assessment: Kan et al. report the discovery of a Bacillus amyloliquifaciens strain that kills Nerisseria gonorrhoeae via oxydifficidin which targets ribosomal proteins. Resistance occurred via mutation in the DedA flippase to influence oxydifficidin uptake. The overall mechanism of action is well described making this an important study with implications for combating clinical antibiotic resistance. The evidence presented is convincing due to rigour employed in the methodological approach. The authors should consider performing a more comprehensive genetic analyses of DedA and RpIL in this clinically relevant strain. This work will be of broad interest to microbiologists and synthetic biologists.
